## How it works

- [statement] PD-related swallowing impairment can cause aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition and dehydration; assessment and rehabilitation therefore address safety and nutrition as well as symptoms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2784698/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] Saliva-reducing botulinum toxin can cause dry mouth and dysphagia: these were reported in SIAXI and among the common adverse events in the rimabotulinumtoxinB adult trial. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurol/articlepdf/10.1001/jamaneurol.2019.4565
- [statement] PD dysarthria can involve reduced volume, monotone pitch, imprecise articulation, altered voice quality and irregular rhythm; it is described as a motor feature even when included in a broader non-motor symptom review. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] SIAXI randomized 184 adults, including 70.7% with PD, to placebo or incobotulinumtoxinA 75 U or 100 U; the 100 U group improved salivary flow and patient global impression at week 4, with a lasting effect at week 16. These are mixed-population results. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] NICE recommends speech and language therapy for Parkinson’s disease when communication, swallowing or saliva problems occur; therapy includes swallowing safety strategies such as EMST and effort-based speech strategies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] NICE recommends considering medication for drooling when non-drug management is unavailable or ineffective, considering glycopyrronium bromide and specialist referral for botulinum toxin A. It restricts other anticholinergics to people judged at minimal cognitive-adverse-effect risk. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] NICE advises considering augmentative and alternative communication equipment as Parkinson’s disease progresses and communication needs change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] SIAXI’s population was 70.7% PD, so its overall results are not PD-only estimates. Treatment-related dry mouth occurred in 5.4% and 2.7%, and dysphagia in 2.7% and 0.0%, of the 75 U and 100 U groups respectively; these findings do not imply swallowing risk is absent. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 2010 blinded sham-controlled trial, 60 participants with PD completed four weeks of EMST or sham training; active EMST improved videofluoroscopic penetration–aspiration scores and hyolaryngeal function compared with sham. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] The rimabotulinumtoxinB trial describes neurological sialorrhea, including PD, as usually reflecting inefficient elimination of oral saliva rather than increased saliva production. (low confidence) — https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurol/articlepdf/10.1001/jamaneurol.2019.4565 · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] In PD COMM (2024), LSVT LOUD reduced self-reported voice handicap at three months versus no therapy by 8.0 points and versus NHS speech and language therapy by 9.6 points; NHS therapy showed no evidence of benefit over no therapy in this trial. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] Evidence appraisal differs by level: Troche’s trial reported improved swallowing safety after EMST, whereas Gandhi and Steele’s systematic review characterized intervention evidence as low certainty and found that lower-risk-of-bias studies supported efficiency benefits rather than safety benefits. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9159671/
- [statement] In PD COMM, 388 people with PD and dysarthria were randomized. LSVT LOUD used four 50-minute sessions weekly for four weeks plus home practice, and reduced self-reported voice handicap at three months versus no therapy by 8.0 points (99% confidence interval −13.3 to −2.6). (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] PD COMM found no evidence of voice-handicap benefit for the trial’s NHS speech and language therapy arm versus no therapy. It recorded 93 adverse events with LSVT LOUD and 46 with NHS therapy, predominantly vocal strain, with no serious adverse events; the trial was unblinded and used a self-reported primary outcome. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] The sialorrhea review attributes PD drooling mainly to impaired saliva clearance and reduced swallowing rather than increased saliva production; cited sialometry studies found reduced production relative to people without PD. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6651/12/11/691 · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] The SIAXI trial, which included adults with PD and other neurological conditions, found incobotulinumtoxinA 100 U improved salivary flow and patient global change versus placebo at week 4, with effects observed at week 16. NICE supports specialist consideration of botulinum toxin A for drooling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The dysphagia consensus recommends instrumental assessment to guide treatment; the management review recommends video fluoroscopy or video endoscopy in severe PD to adjust food and liquid consistency. (medium confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022510X21027040 · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995701/
- [statement] Short-term swallowing improvements should not be interpreted as establishing comparative or durable superiority of dysphagia therapies: the 2020 systematic review found insufficient evidence to compare techniques, and the 2021 consensus found the treatment literature mainly Class IV. (medium confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/17/11/4104 · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022510X21027040
- [statement] Dopaminergic medication does not reliably normalize swallowing: the management review states that swallowing does not necessarily improve, while the dysphagia consensus describes antiparkinsonian drug effects as controversial. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995701/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022510X21027040
- [statement] Botulinum toxin A and B have treatment evidence for PD drooling: the 2019 MDS review rated both efficacious and clinically useful with specialized monitoring, while SIAXI demonstrated benefit of incobotulinumtoxinA in a mixed neurological population that included PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/
- [statement] PD COMM recorded 93 adverse events with LSVT LOUD and 46 with NHS speech and language therapy, predominantly vocal strain, with no serious adverse events. Most participants had early PD and mild speech impairment; allocation was unblinded and participant or carer expectations could bias questionnaire outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] In a sham-controlled randomized trial, 60 participants completed four weeks of EMST or sham training; EMST improved penetration–aspiration scores and hyolaryngeal function. NICE includes EMST among swallowing safety strategies. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] The EMST trial mainly enrolled people with mild to moderate swallowing impairment; its authors explicitly stated that prevention of aspiration pneumonia, durability and maintenance requirements still needed study. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

## Research summary — PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

The cited sources describe specialist assessment and targeted treatment for PD swallowing, saliva and communication problems. Swallowing impairment can cause aspiration pneumonia and nutritional harm; instrumental assessment guides management. EMST has short-term swallowing trial evidence, but comparative and long-term dysphagia treatment evidence remains limited. Botulinum toxin has randomized evidence for drooling, with dry mouth and dysphagia reported as adverse events. LSVT LOUD improved participant-reported voice handicap in PD COMM, although vocal strain and trial design limit interpretation. Speech and language therapy also addresses communication strategies and changing equipment needs.

## Source disagreement — PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

Troche’s positive EMST swallowing-safety result coexists with Gandhi and Steele’s cautious systematic-review conclusion that lower-risk-of-bias studies supported efficiency rather than safety benefits; this is an evidence-certainty difference, not proof the trial result is false.
